text:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created: p99 tail latency spike + streaming stalls affecting SSE/WebSocket clients in eu-west-1. Auto-paged to oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered (SEV2) — high p99 for streaming responses across proxy fleet; 30% of client connections reporting stalled chunks.

Alex: I’m oncall. Looking at traces now. Noted spike at 15:03 UTC, sustained ~6m.

Rita: I see a correlated increase in proxy write queue lengths on proxy-pool-eu-2. SSE connections show many 0-byte writes then long pauses.

Mike: Can we confirm whether backend inference nodes are slow or proxy is the bottleneck?

Alex: Initial tail traces show normal model latencies. The stall happens between proxy and clients — write() syscalls backlog.

Lin: Checking infra metrics — connection pool exhaustion on proxy instances: ephemeral sockets ~500/500 for a subset. Kernel send buffers high.

Rita: Sounds like client backpressure — proxy tries to push chunks but clients aren’t reading; probe shows a surge of long-polling clients in a few customer apps.

Jordan: Customer Success: one customer reported UI hanging and many reconnects. They called support just now. Affects a handful of top-tier customers.

Jen: Support: collecting request IDs and example client traces from customers. Got one L3 debug bundle from customer A.

Alex: Mitigation plan: 1) offload traffic from saturated proxies (weight 0 in LB) 2) increase proxy keepalive timeout and adjust write buffer limits 3) apply temporary circuit-break to very slow clients. Doing step 1 now.

Rita: I’ll prepare a hotfix to reduce proxy-per-connection buffer allocation (config proxy.max_write_buf_bytes -> 64k from 256k) and enable aggressive backpressure detection.

Mike: Rolling a drain on proxy-pool-eu-2 now: LB weights -> 0 for 3 hosts with highest ephemeral usage. This should move new connections away.

Alex: Confirming new connections are going to eu-1 and eu-3, p99 purple line dropping slightly.

Lin: Applying ephemeral socket reclaim script on those 3 hosts to free stale FDs.

incident-bot: Action taken: host weight updates and reclaim script executed.

Rita: Pushing config change as a canary to one proxy host (proxy-eu-2b). If stable for 2m, push to remainder.

Mike: Canary went green after ~45s. No new stalled-chunk alerts on that host. Rolling to the rest of drained hosts in a controlled window.

Alex: Customer-facing update? Jordan/Jen, can we send a short note: "We saw streaming stalls due to proxy-side connection pool pressure; mitigation in progress — reducing buffer sizes and redistributing traffic"

Jordan: Drafting message. Will include ETA ~15–30m for full mitigation and note potential brief reconnects.

Jen: Support has queued the affected customer bundles to the eng runtime team — sending links in #support-escalations.

Rita: After rolling change, observed write() latency drops and chunk success rates climb from 70% -> 98% across the fleet. Still seeing a smaller tail — investigating slow clients causing per-connection blocking.

Alex: For slow clients, we should enable per-connection idle chunk timeout (currently off). I’ll enable a 30s idle chunk timeout with a soft close to allow graceful reconnects.

Mike: Enabled timeout via feature flag on the proxies. Monitoring.

Lin: Noted an oddity in NAT gateway metrics — bursts of SYN retries from a subset of customer IP blocks. Could be flaky networks amplifying client-side backpressure.

Rita: Good call — that explains why certain customers were hit harder. We should add client-side guidance: reduce simultaneous long-lived SSE streams and enable reconnect backoff.

Alex: Handing off to daytime oncall in 20m. Current status: mitigations applied; p99 improved from 3.8s -> 230ms on streaming responses; stalled-chunk alerts down to noise. Remaining actions for follow-up: detailed postmortem, customer RCA, add proxy healthcheck to detect pool exhaustion, tune default write buffer, and assess NAT gateway behavior.

Mike: Logging action items in #postmortems. I’ll take the follow-up owner for adding healthcheck.

Rita: I’ll own the runtime config changes and PR for default buffer reduction + backpressure detection tests.

Lin: I’ll coordinate with cloud provider on NAT anomalies and collect flow logs for the affected intervals.

Jordan: Sending customer note now.

Alex: Handoff to next oncall @Sam in 20m — Sam, summary: proxy connection pool exhaustion + client backpressure -> temporary stalls. Mitigations applied: traffic redistribution, buffer reduction, per-conn idle timeout, ephemeral reclaim. Monitoring looks stable.

Jen: Support awaiting final status before closing escalations.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 transitioned to "Mitigated" by Alex at 15:19 UTC. Post-incident review requested.

Alex: Adding replayable diagnostic commands used in triage:
```
# check send queue lengths
sudo ss -tin state established dst :443 | grep -E "bytes_queued|sendq"

# ephemeral fd usage
cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l || ss -s

# proxy write buffer stats (app-specific)
curl -s -G http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep proxy_write_buf
```

Rita: Noted lessons: default per-connection buffers too large for heavy SSE workloads; add adaptive allocation and detect zero-byte write patterns.

Alex: Nice work team. Will schedule a follow-up postmortem. If anyone finds lingering errors, ping me directly.

Jordan: Customers updated. One asked for a post-incident call — will coordinate next week.

Mike: Closing the Slack incident thread in 1h unless new alerts crop up.

Alex: Handoff complete.
